topic: Keynote Address: A Gig for Every Engineer
title: Keynote Address: A Gig for Every Engineer
session_title: Engineering Education Reimagined: Industrial Gigs and Workforce Readiness-2025 Management Award Session
abstract: The world is changing—and so must the U.S. education system. As technology accelerates change in the workplace, students need clearer pathways from education to employment, along with opportunities to meet experienced professionals and explore career options early. This session brings together leaders in experiential, project-based learning to ask: Why can’t every engineering student have meaningful engagement with potential employers integrated into their academic journey? We propose a connected model—from high school through to the workforce—that enables continuous skill development, real-world problem-solving, and tighter links between research, market needs, and back again. With cycle times from idea to application shrinking, universities must reimagine how students engage in research and innovation. Scalable models like industrial gigs—short, skills-focused collaborations with industry—can help students gain experience, build critical capabilities, and contribute to innovation pipelines. These efforts promote readiness, relevance, and competitiveness for both students and the nation.

topic: Panel: The Significance of Practical Experience for Students
title: Panel: The Significance of Practical Experience for Students
session_title: Engineering Education Reimagined: Industrial Gigs and Workforce Readiness-2025 Management Award Session
abstract: The panel discussion will explore the importance of practical experience in the educational journey of engineering students. Emphasis will be placed on the application of theoretical knowledge to real-world problem-solving, early exposure to a variety of industrial research opportunities, and the ability for students to explore career options early on. Key discussion points will include: - The critical role of skill acquisition, particularly soft skills, in enhancing students' professional readiness as they transition into the engineering workforce. - Industrial gigs as a low-cost method for companies to execute initiatives and facilitate hiring through industry contacts. - Workforce development strategies aimed at creating a pipeline of job-ready graduates with hands-on experience, thereby strengthening workforce competitiveness. - Bridging the skills gap in rapidly evolving sectors and boosting innovation. The session will also discuss challenges faced by the U.S. education system, such as student engagement in engineering, high costs, and the perceived decreasing returns on investment in university education.

topic: The inside Gig: How Sharing Untapped Talent across Boundaries Unleashes Organizational Capacity
title: The inside Gig: How Sharing Untapped Talent across Boundaries Unleashes Organizational Capacity
session_title: Engineering Education Reimagined: Industrial Gigs and Workforce Readiness-2025 Management Award Session
abstract: The Inside Gig provides an innovative approach to talent management by harnessing the untapped skills within an organization. This session will demonstrate how the establishment of a talent marketplace can enhance employee engagement, promote continuous learning, improve organizational agility, and reduce costs. The strategic deployment of existing workforce capabilities in the form of a marketplace addresses the evolving war for talent and the need for re-skilling in response to rapid technological advancements. Through the recommendations discussed, organizations can optimize their workforce by leveraging internal skills across boundaries, thereby minimizing external dependency. The Inside Gig is essential for businesses aiming to thrive in the future marketplace by effectively utilizing their internal talent pool.

title: Engineering Tomorrow
session_title: Engineering Education Reimagined: Industrial Gigs and Workforce Readiness-2025 Management Award Session
abstract: Engineering Tomorrow, a non-profit founded in 2014, aims to address the critical shortage of engineers by inspiring a diverse high school community to explore the exciting opportunities and careers an engineering education can offer. Through engaging labs based on today’s global issues and new technologies, the organization introduces students to various engineering fields and challenges including access to clean water, renewable energy, electric vehicles, decarbonization and green hydrogen, machine learning and 3D printing. By offering no-cost labs nationwide through a combination of free lab kits, live engagement with professional engineers, and speakers who are leaders in their field, our goal is to diversify the engineering workforce and fill the future engineering workforce pipeline. In this talk, we will discuss how our model works and how it may be expanded to provide support to students by facilitating “real-world” problem solving and experiences.

topic: Path Forward: A Gig for Every Engineering Student
title: Path Forward: A Gig for Every Engineering Student
session_title: Engineering Education Reimagined: Industrial Gigs and Workforce Readiness-2025 Management Award Session
abstract: Engineering education must evolve to meet rapid advances in technology and shifting workforce needs. This talk presents a scalable model that integrates learning, leadership, and innovation through real-world problems, industry engagement, and AI-enabled tools. Designed for chemical engineering students and educators, the approach emphasizes horizontal integration across education and employment, fostering career clarity, adaptive skills, and innovation mindsets. The model is being piloted with universities and companies to prepare the next generation of engineers for impact in a fast-changing world.
